title: IDEA: A Flexible Framework of Certified Unlearning for Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Trained GNNs may encode sensitive personal information in their parameters, creating a risk of privacy leakage when deployed.

gap.claim: Existing certified GNN unlearning methods generally handle only node and edge requests and are tailored to specific GNN designs or training objectives, limiting flexibility.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes IDEA, a framework for flexible and certified unlearning in GNNs.
IDEA instantiates four types of graph unlearning requests and uses an approximation approach to handle them across diverse GNNs.
The paper provides a theoretical guarantee certifying the effectiveness of the proposed unlearning approach.

stated_novelty.claim: Unlike existing alternatives, IDEA is not designed for a specific GNN or optimization objective and is intended to generalize easily.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets report superiority for IDEA across multiple key perspectives.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are widely deployed, while their training data may contain sensitive personal information.
Sensitive information can be encoded in trained GNN parameters and exposed through privacy leakage.
Machine unlearning, especially certified unlearning, aims to remove personal information with theoretical effectiveness guarantees.
Existing certified methods have limited request coverage and flexibility across GNN designs and training objectives.
IDEA addresses flexibility through multiple request types, diverse-GNN handling, certification, and reported real-world dataset experiments.

source_observation.claim: Existing certified unlearning approaches are limited by narrow request coverage and dependence on particular model designs or objectives.

interpretation.claim: A flexible unlearning system should vary both the supported request types and the underlying GNN or training objective.

application.claim: When designing privacy-removal mechanisms for graph models, support multiple graph-level request types and avoid unnecessary coupling to one architecture or objective.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that architecture- or objective-agnostic designs are optimal for every deployment setting.

unknowns: The four unlearning request types are not enumerated.
The approximation method and certification theorem are not specified.
The evaluated datasets, baselines, metrics, and reported superiority perspectives are not described.
The privacy threat model and attacker capabilities are not specified.
